text.p: Italian debt markets powered higher as renewed optimism about the prospects for European monetary union, a stronger lira and a firmer Bund market gave them fresh upward impetus.
The June Btp future on LIFFE was 204 basis points higher at 127.66, almost the day's high, after the cash market closed.
The February 2007 Btp ended 145 basis points ahead at 94.75, yielding 7.64 percent and with a spread over 10-year Bunds of 175 basis points.
The lira seized old ground from the mark, pressing to 984.70/5.00 in late trade from 990 late on Friday.
The lira was at the highest levels since mid-February.

"The Btp has had a very good run since this morning. It's broken one technical resistance after another," one broker in London commented. "We're trading up on the back of the strong currency and hopes of EMU starting on time."
Markets took heart from an Ecofin meeting which indicated the will to keep the EMU timetable on track is hardening.

Italian Treasury Minister Crlo Azeglio Ciampi also said at the weekend Italian inflation would fall to 1.9 percent year-on-year shortly and consumer price inflation may stabilise at 1.5 percent at the end of June.

Dealers said speculation was also starting to creep into the market that the Bank of Italy might have room to ease official interest rates in the coming month or so, perhaps after preliminary inflation data for April, given the lira's recovery.
Others however said while the speculation mighyt be creeping they themselves were sceptical the central bank would ease in the medium term.
